analysis.evidence: לֶמֶךְ is the subject of וַיְחִי. The verse counts the 595 years Lamech lived after he fathered Noah.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated verb form.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לֶמֶךְ with its derivation left open.
draft.definition: A masculine personal name borne here by the son of Methuselah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:26 identifies Lamech by naming him as the son whom Methuselah fathered.

analysis.evidence: לֶמֶךְ is the subject of וַיְחִי, “he lived.” The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת נֹחַ, “after he fathered Noah,” identifies him as Noah’s father, the same Lamech whom Methuselah fathered in Genesis 5:25–26.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי governs הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת נֹחַ, “his fathering Noah.” The phrase marks the event after which Lamech lived another 595 years.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת נֹחַ, “after he fathered Noah,” the suffix refers to Lamech, and אֶת marks Noah as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine singular subject suffix ־וֹ

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת נֹחַ (“after he fathered Noah”), אֶת marks the personal name נֹחַ as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ. Lamech is the one who fathered Noah.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת נֹחַ, “after he fathered Noah,” אֶת marks נֹחַ as the direct object. Lamech is the father, and Noah is the son he named in the preceding verse.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In חָמֵשׁ וְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה, חָמֵשׁ supplies the five in “five and ninety years.” Its feminine form agrees with שָׁנָה.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Gen.5.30 as an example of the existing ninety sense in tesha.
draft.definition: The cardinal number ninety, nine tens.
draft.evidence: Gen.5.30 joins five to ninety in counting the years Lamech lived after Noah’s birth.

analysis.evidence: In חָמֵשׁ וְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה, ‘five and ninety years’, the marked numeral supplies the ninety in ninety-five. The following וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאֹת שָׁנָה adds five hundred years, giving 595 years of Lamech’s life after Noah’s birth.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ ‘and’ + cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: In חָמֵשׁ וְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for ‘ninety-five.’ Together with the following five hundred years, it measures how long Lamech lived after he fathered Noah.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאֹת שָׁנָה, the marked numeral counts hundreds. The conjunction adds five hundred years to the preceding ninety-five, giving 595 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral.

analysis.evidence: In וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאֹת שָׁנָה, חֲמֵשׁ counts five hundreds, giving “and five hundred years.” Together with the preceding ninety-five years, this gives 595 years.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאֹת שָׁנָה, “and five hundred years,” the marked noun supplies the unit for five hundred. Together with the preceding ninety-five years, it measures the 595 years Lamech lived after fathering Noah.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Lamech is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת (“sons and daughters”) are its direct objects.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix
